result.planSummary: Addressed verifier findings SV-03-01 and SV-03-02. SQLite row-level turn/chunk writes now merge higher-trust token-derived fields from the current row before persisting stale same-row maintenance updates, preserving newer exact/provider-derived state. Background maintenance fixed counts now come from resolved maintenance debt between the initial and final snapshots, so already-clean runs report zero fixed rows. Targeted Story 3 tests and typecheck pass; the configured `npm run verify-all` gate failed in an unrelated PI E2E setup command timeout with no stdout/stderr/fetch log, and the narrow failing E2E rerun reproduced the same timeout.

changedFiles.reason: Added optional row-level turn/chunk write contracts and maintenance-status persistence contract for stores.
Extended thread status with maintenance run records and debt metadata for inspectable bounded/manual repair status.
Implemented SQLite row-level turn/chunk mutation methods and added same-row derived token metadata merging so stale row writers preserve newer higher-trust persisted fields.
Switched bounded token maintenance to row-level writes, persisted maintenance run status, and changed background fixed counts to actual resolved maintenance debt instead of hard-coded phase counts.
Used row-level turn writes for smooth persistence when available.
Used row-level turn writes for lower-band projection persistence when available.
Used row-level chunk writes for chunk-state refreshes and refined transcript-change handling so semantic artifacts are not invalidated on no-op refreshes.
Used row-level chunk writes for semantic artifact persistence and queued async compression via an unref’d timer so short-lived PI runs can exit cleanly.
Persisted full manual-repair maintenance status after success/failure.
Added reusable SQLite maintenance fixture and fake exact-token counter helpers for Story 3 coverage.
Added bounded background maintenance, stale canonical write coverage, dependent chunk readiness coverage, and follow-up turn/chunk same-row lost-update regression probes.
Added full manual repair success/failure coverage with persisted maintenance status assertions.
Added thread-level maintenance reporting coverage, bounded-vs-manual distinction, and follow-up already-clean background no-op fixed-count coverage.
Extended token tests to cover exact SQLite repair metadata persistence and partial-repair debt visibility.

gatesRun.command: node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "^e2e: status and turn-health commands$|^/lh-status and /lh-turn-health execute as commands, not model prompts$" tests/context-steward/e2e-cli.e2e.test.ts

findingsFixed: SV-03-01: SQLite row-level turn writes now preserve newer higher-trust raw/smooth/lower-band projection token metadata when a stale same-row derived writer persists another field from an older snapshot.
SV-03-01: SQLite row-level chunk writes now preserve newer higher-trust chunk smooth/detailed/brief token metadata when a stale same-row derived writer persists another field from an older snapshot.
SV-03-02: Background maintenance fixedCount now reports resolved maintenance debt, so already-clean no-op runs persist fixedCount 0 instead of fabricated phase counts.
findingsSurfaced: The configured `npm run verify-all` gate failed after Story 3 targeted tests passed because `tests/context-steward/e2e-cli.e2e.test.ts` timed out during the setup prompt for `e2e: status and turn-health commands`; the preserved PI run log had empty stdout/stderr and no fetch log, and a narrow rerun reproduced the same PI exit-code 124 timeout.

openQuestions: Should the repeated PI E2E setup timeout be treated as an external/runtime flake and rerun separately, or should a follow-up story triage that command setup path outside Story 3 scope?
result.recommendedNextStep: Have the verifier or a human rerun/triage the isolated PI E2E timeout; the SV-03-01 and SV-03-02 fixes are covered by passing targeted tests and typecheck.
